newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Minerals chief exit flags BHP coal shakeup.
newsitem.headline: Minerals chief exit flags BHP coal shakeup.

text.p: The sudden departure of the Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd (BHP) Minerals Division chief, Dick Carter, signalled a major shakeup for the group's coal assets, analysts said on Wednesday.
"In terms of BHP's coal operations something has to give, productivity is just too low," a Melbourne-based analyst said.

The analyst speculated the timing of the announcement of Carter's retirement along with a statement saying the results of the last phase of BHP's strategic review would be announced in the next few weeks, heralded big changes for Carter's division.
"I'm not sure if he (Carter) has been pushed or whether he is not agreeing with some of the decisions that are being made. That is all speculation," a Melbourne-based analyst said.
Another analyst said BHP was strong on succession planning and the fact the company had not announced a replacement suggested that Carter's exit was unexpected.

In a brief, two paragraph statement, BHP said Carter, the executive general manager of BHP Minerals, was to retire from August 31 and that an announcement about appointments following his retirement would be made sooon.
A spokesman from BHP said Carter was not commenting on his departure and said the resignation had not been previously foreshadowed by the company.

BHP managing director John Prescott earlier said most effort was being directed at lifting the coal division's performance and ensuring that the large number of new projects in the division were commissioned as effectively as possible.
Last week the company dismissed as speculative a newspaper report which said it was likely to sell its interest in three thermal coal mines in Queensland.
The report in the Australian newspaper said the company was believed to have approached joint venture parteners in the mines to secure consent to sell its interests.
Newspapers also have widely speculated that the company plans to sell its Mt Owen thermal coal mine in the Hunter Valley in New South Wales.

In June this year BHP signalled its intention to focus on the coking coal market by spending A$500 million expanding the Peak Downs and Sarji open-cut coking coal mines in Queensland and the port of Hays Point.
